newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan power utilities sign reprocessing agreement.
newsitem.headline: Japan power utilities sign reprocessing agreement.

text.p: Japan's 10 main power utilities have signed an agreement consigning nuclear fuel reprocessing to Japan Nuclear Fuel Ltd (JNFL) when its plant begins operating in 2003, a JNFL spokesman said on Wednesday.
The spokesman said details, such as the terms and volumes covered by the agreement, were still under negotiation.
He added that there were no plans for JNFL to accept consignments from overseas.
JNFL is currently constructing a reprocessing facility at Rokkashomura, Aomori prefecture, some 700 kilometres (km) north of Tokyo.
Japan's Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) reprocesses a small amount of spent fuel at its Tokaimura plant in Ibaraki Prefecture, north of Tokyo.
JNFL's facility will have the capacity to reprocess 800 tonnes of uranium a year and will be Japan's first major commercial nuclear fuel reprocessing plant when it begins operating.
The bulk of Japanese power utilities' spent nuclear fuel is currently reprocessed overseas in either Britain or France.
Nuclear power supplies some 30 percent of Japan's electricity.

There is growing public distrust towards Japan's nuclear energy policy, however, particularly after a recent string of accidents at PNC's Tokaimura reprocessing plant and other nuclear power-related facilities.
